report.summary:
The supplied candidate had a real defect, and I fixed it with a one-character edit. The original 29-byte generated/hello-world.mjs (sha256 647697a5…4993) contained `console.log("Hello world!");` with no comma. I ran `node generated/hello-world.mjs` from the project root on Node v24.7.0 and piped stdout to od. It printed the 13 bytes "Hello world!\n" and exited 0. The original source and basic-cli.oracle.json require "Hello, world!\n", so the output was wrong.

The fix adds the comma: `console.log("Hello, world!");` followed by a newline. The file is now 30 bytes (sha256 fe8f4080…e9ef). Running it again printed exactly the 14 bytes "Hello, world!\n" and exited 0, with no package installation.

As a self-check I also ran the plan's command, `node --test test/component/hello-cli.test.mjs test/uat/hello-cli.uat.test.mjs`. It exited 0 with tests 2, pass 2, fail 0. These are my own runs, not admitted evidence or independent acceptance.

No other file was changed. I wrote nothing to disk while checking; all output went through pipes. The empty operator-scratch/tmp directory was already there when I started, so I left it in place.
